title: RCB Against Gujarat in Ahmedabad Tonight. The IPL 2026 Final Is Here.
excerpt: Defending champions Royal Challengers Bengaluru seek back-to-back titles against a Gujarat Titans side that has won five of seven home matches this season. First ball at 7:30 PM IST.
body:
Two months. Seventy-three matches. Ten franchises. And now it comes down to one night in Ahmedabad.

Royal Challengers Bengaluru will play Gujarat Titans in the IPL 2026 final at the Narendra Modi Stadium on Sunday evening, with the first ball scheduled for 7:30 PM IST. RCB are chasing history — a back-to-back title that would put them alongside Mumbai Indians and Chennai Super Kings as the only franchises to defend the IPL crown. Gujarat are chasing redemption, returning to the final after being demolished by 92 runs in Qualifier 1 five days ago.

## How They Got Here

RCB's path to the final has been the more commanding of the two. They finished first in the league phase with nine wins from thirteen matches, then crushed Gujarat in Qualifier 1 with a playoff-record total of 254 for 5. Rajat Patidar's unbeaten 93 was the centrepiece of that innings — an exhibition of controlled aggression that reduced GT's bowling attack to spectators.

Gujarat's route has been harder. After the Qualifier 1 humiliation, they had to travel to Mullanpur for Qualifier 2 against Rajasthan Royals. There, Shubman Gill answered his critics with a magnificent 104 off 53 balls, chasing down 215 with eight balls to spare. It was Gill's second century in the playoffs and a captain's knock in the truest sense. But the turnaround came at a cost — severe weather delayed GT's flight from Chandigarh to Ahmedabad on Saturday, leaving the team with less than 24 hours of preparation time before the final.

RCB, by contrast, arrived in Ahmedabad on Wednesday.

## The Key Match-Ups

**Bhuvneshwar Kumar vs GT's top order.** RCB's seam spearhead has 26 wickets this season and has dismissed Gill five times and Jos Buttler nine times across their careers. His first four overs could define the contest.

**Kagiso Rabada vs Virat Kohli.** The Purple Cap holder has dismissed Kohli five times. The South African's pace and bounce at the Narendra Modi Stadium — where the pitch has historically offered more for the quicks — could trouble RCB's marquee batter. Jason Holder has also dismissed Kohli four times.

**Rashid Khan vs Devdutt Padikkal.** The Afghan leg-spinner has had the better of Padikkal on five occasions. If GT can get through the powerplay without significant damage, Rashid's middle-overs spell could be the squeeze that turns the match.

## The Venue Factor

Gujarat have turned Ahmedabad into a fortress this season, winning five of their seven home matches. The Narendra Modi Stadium — the largest cricket venue in the world, with a capacity of over 130,000 — holds special memories for both franchises. GT lifted their maiden trophy here in 2022. RCB ended their eighteen-year wait for silverware on the same ground last year.

"Yes, physically they might have an advantage," Gill said of RCB's extra preparation time. "But I think finals are all about mental strength, so the team that is mentally up there for the challenge is the one that's going to win."

## The NRI Watch Guide

The final will be broadcast live on Star Sports channels in India, with JioHotstar providing live streaming. For NRI viewers:

- **United States and Canada:** Willow TV and JioHotstar International
- **United Kingdom:** Sky Sports Cricket
- **Australia:** Fox Cricket
- **Middle East:** OSN Sports
- **Kick-off time:** 7:30 PM IST / 10:00 AM ET / 7:00 AM PT / 3:00 PM BST / 12:00 AM AEST (Monday)

## What's at Stake

For RCB, this is about legacy. A second consecutive title would cement Patidar's captaincy as one of the most successful in franchise history and give Kohli, now 37, another chapter in his IPL story. For Gujarat, it is about identity. The Titans have reached three finals in five years of existence — no franchise has matched that strike rate. A win would confirm them as the IPL's defining team of the 2020s.

The head-to-head record is dead even at the margins — RCB lead 5-4 in nine meetings — and the three encounters this season have produced two RCB victories and one GT win. Momentum favours Bengaluru. Conditions favour Gujarat. The trophy will go to whichever side imposes its game first.
